_about: Invented sample. Every person, company and exchange here is fictional. Run the tracker with --as-of 2026-10-07T09:00:00+00:00 to reproduce the documented output; it contains one thread in every state.

threads.post_topic: Removing the kickoff call from onboarding
threads.post_ref: Harbourline VP CS, post of 6 Oct
threads.comment: The enterprise split matches what we saw. We dropped our kickoff for accounts under 50 seats last year and nobody blinked.

events.note: Asked whether the short call for large accounts is run by sales or by success

threads.post_ref: CFO at Northmere, post of 4 Oct
threads.comment: Our finance buyers accepted usage pricing once the invoice showed a ceiling. Without the ceiling, three of five stalled in procurement.

events.note: Wanted to know how the ceiling was set and whether anyone hit it

threads.post_topic: Why her team stopped doing quarterly business reviews
threads.comment: We replaced ours with a one-page note sent two days before renewal conversations. Attendance stopped being the measure.

events.note: Asked to see the structure of the one-page note

threads.comment: We hired ours too late, after the third pricing change. What did the first ninety days look like for yours?

threads.post_topic: Annual versus monthly billing for small clinics
threads.post_ref: Founder of Pellow Health, post of 3 Oct
threads.comment: Monthly kept clinics under five staff from churning in their first year for us; annual only worked once they had a practice manager.

events.note: Asked what share of small clinics moved to annual later
Answered: about a third, mostly at the second renewal

threads.post_topic: Dunning emails that do not sound like threats
threads.comment: The version that worked best for us named the person who would call, with a day. Recovery went up and complaints went down.
We learned the hard way to keep intercompany accounts out of the operating ranges from day one.

threads.post_topic: Refund policy as a sales tool
threads.post_ref: Head of Sales at Quillfield, post of 28 Sep
threads.comment: A no-questions refund in the first sixty days cost us under two percent of revenue and removed the longest objection in our calls.

events.note: Answered: four cases in a year, all under a month old
Said he would test it on the mid-market plan
Suggested starting with the plan that has the most trial-to-paid friction

threads.comment: Seats still work for us where every seat is a named clinician. It breaks when one login is shared by a front desk.

events.name: Lars Oedegaard
events.note: Disagreed: says named seats only hold under about fifty users

threads.comment: The part that surprised us was credit notes, not invoices. They took four times the engineering effort.

events.note: Asked for an example of a credit-note edge case

closed.reason: She messaged; continued by direct message

threads.post_topic: Why her finance team rejects tools without an audit trail
threads.post_ref: Controller at Brackenridge Group, post of 5 Oct
threads.comment: We lost two deals before we understood that the audit trail had to be exportable, not just visible.

events.note: Asked which export format the auditors accepted
Answered: a dated CSV per period plus a signed summary
Asked whether the summary was signed by us or by the customer
Answered: by the customer's controller, we only generate it
Said that matches what her auditors want and thanked me
